source.title: To Call or Not to Call: Diagnosing Intrinsic Over-Calling Bias in LLM Agents
source.authors: Wei Shi; Ziheng Peng; Sihang Li; Xi-Ting Wang; Xiang Wang; Meng-Nan Du; Na Zou

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether sparse, behavior-aligned features can be recovered from LLM activations with SAEs, using feature-probe AUROC rather than the original toy-model superposition method. It does not directly test superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports tool-call/no-call accuracy, an activation-margin bias diagnosis, and steering outcomes. These concern tool-use gating and its correction, not the listed superposition versions, so they are not recorded as rows. The SAE probe results are reported in aggregate across six models; exact AUROC values are not stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study uses TopK SAEs as a tool to diagnose an over-calling bias in tool-using LLMs. The probe results in Section 3.3 validate the authors' own feature-selection pipeline: ranked SAE features are compared with random SAE features and a raw-residual probe. They do not test whether LLM features are superposed, spread across neurons, or sparse in a way that bears on V4. No toy models, polysemanticity analysis, feature canonicity or feature dimensionality are examined.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that over-calling reflects an activation-independent CALL offset (negative neutral boundary in all six models), which they diagnose with behaviour-aligned SAE features. Steering along SAE decoder directions (AMCS) counteracts it on most models, but not on Gemma. They draw no conclusions about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: Uses TopK SAEs, behavior-labeled feature ranking, logistic probes, and activation steering on LLM residual streams; it does not use the original toy-network superposition setup or its geometry measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe results are compared across feature counts and differ between discovered and random SAE features. The paper also reports that SAE feature geometry varies by family, with Gemma features dispersed and Qwen3.5/Ministral features clustered; this is not a test of superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: A handful of behaviour-ranked SAE features (typically K≤5) predict CALL/NO_CALL decisions near a raw-residual linear probe, while random SAE features stay near chance, across six LLMs. This is reported in Fig. 3 without exact values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-specific decision signals in LLM residual streams are concentrated in a few SAE dictionary features.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 is stated in the paper; venue metadata also identifies arXiv.org.
record.problems: For the V4 result, exact AUROC values are only shown in Figure 3 and are not stated in the text. The study measures tool-decision features, not general feature geometry, neuron overlap, or superposition.
record.rows_left_out: No separate per-model probe rows were extracted because the text summarizes the result across all six models and does not state their individual values. Tool-use accuracy and AMCS intervention results were omitted because they do not measure the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No toy networks, sparsity-dependent transition, or geometry of superposed features.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity-competition analysis.
No analysis of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Does not measure feature spread across neurons. Does not evaluate SAE recovery of features as evidence of superposition; SAEs are only a diagnostic tool.
SAE retraining (layer, K, seed) is used only to check the robustness of the bias offset. Feature stability, completeness and canonicity are not assessed.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and V4 'supports' label are dropped. The SAE probe results validate the authors' diagnostic basis (the study's own method compared with random features and a raw probe), so they are not evidence on recoverability of superposed features. The Appendix E UMAP geometry (clustered features in Qwen/Ministral, dispersed in Gemma) is also not a superposition test.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-over-dimension setting, sparsity-dependent transition, or superposition geometry are tested.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not investigate polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.

Tests recovery of tool-decision-related SAE features in the examined LLMs, not whether general model features are distributed across neurons or whether SAE recovery provides evidence of superposition.
SAE retraining robustness is used to check the bias diagnosis; the paper does not establish SAE features as complete, stable, or canonical units.
Uses SAE decoder directions but does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Six target models (aggregate: Qwen3.5-4B and 9B, Gemma-3-it-1B and 4B, Ministral-3-Instruct-3B and 8B)
rows.stage_stated: Mixed; Gemma-3-it and Ministral-3-Instruct are named as such; stage for Qwen3.5 is not stated
rows.operation_detail: 5-fold cross-validated logistic probes on selected behavior-aligned SAE features to predict CALL decisions
rows.measure: Mean AUROC for predicting the behavior-labeled gating decision
rows.baseline: Raw residual stream probe, described as the upper bound
rows.value: Across all three model families, discovered SAE features reach the raw-residual upper bound with a handful of features, typically K ≤ 5; exact AUROC not stated in text
rows.note: The paper reports this as an aggregate result across all six models and both decision directions; it does not give exact probe AUROCs in the text.
rows.check: This row reports the study's own feature-selection method against a raw-residual upper bound. It is a validation of the selected feature basis for one behaviour label, not a measure of whether real models contain sparse features an SAE can recover in V4's sense. Values are figure-only.
